turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): sorry, give me a second, the screen's frozen. right. what can I do for you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): umm we were late, I'm all flustered, the bus didn't move for ages.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): sorry doctor, the 49 was awful. shopping's still in the boot I think.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): ok. what's the actual problem?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): burning when I pass water, and I need the loo constantly.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): uh sorry. say that again? an alert just popped up.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): it burns every time I wee, I'm going all the time, and my lower back's aching as well.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): how long?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): four days. the burning, the weeing, the back, all of it, four days.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): he's been up and down all night with it, poor thing.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): and I feel a bit feverish. not flu, just warm, and a bit shivery.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): a temperature? have you felt properly hot?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah, low grade, it comes and goes.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): is it my kidneys? my uncle had kidney trouble and I can't stop thinking about it.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): one thing at a time. any discharge from the penis?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): no. nothing like that.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): been abroad recently? anywhere?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): no, nowhere. I keep meaning to book Spain and the brochures just sit there.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): he lives on his own, I come in every day. he hardly leaves the flat except the chemist.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): any cough, or trouble getting your breath?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): no. no cough, breathing's fine.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): any vomiting, or diarrhoea?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): no, neither. toast and tea, that's been it, which is dull but fine.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): and weight, have you lost any?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): umm I don't think so. well maybe a little, I'm not really sure. the scales are in the cupboard.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): sorry, lost that, the screen flashed. weight, yes or no?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't give you a yes or no. maybe a bit, maybe nothing.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): if it is the kidney will you keep me in? I hate hospitals.
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): while you're in there, he takes tamsolosin every morning, the prostate capsule.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): nought point four milligrams, once a day. started it since Diwali or after, I lose track.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): nought point four, not forty? say it once more, I typed the wrong box.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): nought point four milligrams. one capsule every morning. definitely not forty.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been taking paracetamol as well, for the ache and the heat.
[SEG0034] person_3 (CAREGIVER): two of the five-hundred milligram tablets, three times a day, since this started.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): and trimethoprim, two hundred milligrams twice a day, I stopped it in March. only managed a few days, it made me queasy. it was for a water infection.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): stopped in March. you didn't carry on with it?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): no I stopped it. the ciprofloksacin they printed that time, I never took that, not one tablet.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): true, that prescription is still in the kitchen drawer. he never started those.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): right, enlarged prostate, that's ongoing, I can see it on your record.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah, years of it. and this burning, I had the same last winter, or the one before, I genuinely can't say which.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): should I stop the prostate capsule, is it making the burning worse?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): no, keep taking it. tummy's soft, no guarding. there's a bit of tenderness over the right loin.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): the nurse scribbled these before we came through. blood pressure one eighteen over seventy-six. temperature thirty-seven point six.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): pulse. did she say seventy-eight? I only half caught it.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): no, eighty-eight. pulse eighty-eight. sats ninety-seven percent.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): eighty-eight, got it. last time in March you were sixty-eight, that was the pulse, and your last pressure was one-forty over ninety. we use today's.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is most likely a lower urine infection. the back ache might be referred, though I can't fully rule out an early pyelonephritis.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): so not hospital? is it catching for her? and can I still drink tea?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): not hospital on this. not catching like that. tea's fine. we'll send a urine sample to the lab today.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): what about antibiotics? not the ones that made me sick. what if I'm worse tonight?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): you're well enough to wait. if the culture shows an infection I'll start nitrofurantoin, a hundred milligrams twice a day for seven days. not before the result, and it's not the trimethoprim.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): how much should I make him drink? he forgets the glass is there.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): two to three litres of water if he manages. if he gets shivers he can't control, or he can't keep fluids down, that's A and E. if you're worse tomorrow, come back and we'll see you. otherwise I'll see you in five days for the result.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): is five days soon enough though? sorry, I know I've asked a lot.

spec.situation: Man with burning urine, frequency and lower back ache for four days; fever mild; denies discharge; no recent travel; urine test and antibiotic planned, conditional on result.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
